matchstick.title: Balance by numeric difference and single‑stick transformation
matchstick.principle: First compute the integer values of both sides of the equation (evaluating any arithmetic expressions) and determine the numeric imbalance; then look for a single‑stick change that can adjust the imbalance by exactly that amount.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever the equation is false and you need to decide which stick to move to restore equality.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick arbitrarily without first checking the numeric difference, e.g., guessing a change that yields a true equality but cannot be achieved with one stick.

matchstick.title: Convert V to X to add 5
matchstick.principle: If the numeric imbalance is exactly 5 and a V appears, you can increase its value by 5 by repositioning one of its diagonal sticks to form an X.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to increase a numeral by 5 and a V is present in the equation.
matchstick.example: Converting a V to X when the required adjustment is not 5, e.g., changing V to X in a puzzle where the numeric imbalance is 2, leading to an incorrect total.

matchstick.title: Change + to - and add I
matchstick.principle: To turn a plus sign into a minus sign, remove its vertical stick; then place that stick as a solitary I elsewhere so the total stick count stays the same.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to replace a '+' with a '-' and have a place to put the removed vertical stick as an I.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical stick from '+' to make '-', but not placing that stick elsewhere as an I, leaving an extra stick unused.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: If a numeral contains more than one I (multiple vertical sticks), you can move one of those I sticks to another numeral, adjusting both values by ±1.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric imbalance is 1 and a numeral with extra I's is available to donate a stick.
matchstick.example: Taking the only I from a solitary I numeral, which would eliminate the numeral entirely.

matchstick.title: Change - to = by adding a horizontal stick from a numeral
matchstick.principle: To convert a minus sign into an equals sign you need a second horizontal stick; take that stick from a numeral that can spare a horizontal without becoming invalid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to replace '-' with '=', and a suitable horizontal stick is available elsewhere.
matchstick.example: Taking a horizontal stick from a numeral that has no horizontals (e.g., X) to turn '-' into '=', breaking the source numeral.

matchstick.title: When converting - to +, also move a vertical stick to form a valid plus sign
matchstick.principle: Changing a minus sign to a plus sign requires adding a vertical stick; obtain that vertical stick from a numeral that can lose one (e.g., an I or a numeral with multiple I's).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to replace '-' with '+' and have a vertical stick that can be moved without invalidating its source.
matchstick.example: Turning '-' into '+' without adding the vertical stick, leaving a malformed '+' sign.

matchstick.title: Swap '-' and '=' by moving a horizontal stick
matchstick.principle: If both a minus sign and an equals sign appear, you can exchange them by moving one horizontal stick from the '=' to the '-', turning the minus into '=', and the '=' into '-'.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains both '-' and '=', and swapping them may resolve the numeric imbalance.
matchstick.example: Swapping '-' and '=' without moving any stick, leaving both operators unchanged.

matchstick.title: Ensure a valid '=' remains when moving a stick from '='
matchstick.principle: If you relocate any stick from the equality sign, you must keep two horizontal sticks so that the sign remains a valid '=', otherwise it becomes a minus sign.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to take a stick from '=', make sure you replace it with another horizontal to preserve the equality sign.
matchstick.example: Removing one of the two horizontals from '=', leaving only one horizontal and turning it into a minus sign.

matchstick.title: Convert X to V to subtract 5
matchstick.principle: If the numeric imbalance is exactly 5 and an X appears, you can decrease its value by 5 by removing one of its diagonal sticks, turning the X into a V.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to reduce a numeral by 5 and an X is present in the equation.
matchstick.example: Changing X to V when the needed adjustment is 3, leading to an incorrect total.

matchstick.title: Evaluate expressions when computing numeric imbalance
matchstick.principle: When computing the numeric values of each side, first evaluate any arithmetic expression (e.g., subtraction) to obtain a single integer before comparing the two sides.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving any matchstick equation, especially when the right side (or left side) contains operators like '-' or '+'.
matchstick.example: Treating 'XII - VI' as a string instead of evaluating it to 6, leading to an incorrect assessment of the numeric imbalance.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from a numeral that cannot lose a stick without becoming invalid (e.g., X, V, solitary I)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes any numeral can donate a stick, ignoring the minimal stick requirement for a valid Roman symbol.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Only move sticks from numerals that have at least two sticks of the same type and will remain a valid Roman numeral after removal.

matchstick.description: Providing an invalid equation after moving a stick (including incomplete or unreachable solutions)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on making the equality true numerically but neglects the constraint that the transformation must be achievable with exactly one stick move.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After proposing a solution, verify that the change can be performed by moving exactly one stick: the source symbol must be able to lose a stick and stay valid, and the target symbol must be able to gain it and become a valid symbol.

matchstick.description: Changing – to + without adding the required vertical stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes the horizontal of the minus sign but forgets to add the vertical needed for a plus sign.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When converting '-' to '+', always add a vertical stick from a suitable source (e.g., an extra I) to complete the plus sign.

matchstick.description: Using an angled stick as a vertical stick (or vice versa)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats any stick as interchangeable, ignoring orientation constraints of Roman symbols and operators.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Respect stick orientation: only vertical sticks can form I or the vertical part of '+', only horizontal sticks can form '-' or '=', and only diagonal sticks belong to V or X.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from the equality sign and leaving no valid '=' sign in the equation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a horizontal from '=', forgetting that '=' requires two horizontals to remain a valid equality sign.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: If you take a stick from '=', replace it with another horizontal or avoid taking from '=' unless you also add a horizontal elsewhere to keep it as '='.
